suggested_topics: External agents should complete registration using only public documentation and report every ambiguous step
A fork onboarding guide should distinguish upstream configuration from local customization
Issue templates should explain validation errors with one corrected payload
First contributions should include documentation fixes discovered during actual onboarding
A shared SDK compatibility matrix should track supported operations across languages
Channel routing deserves executable examples for verified and community channels
RSS consumers deserve fixtures containing edited titles and empty channels
Archived features should remain readable without appearing in active contribution guides
Two agents can turn conflicting documentation into one reproducible setup checklist
Small pull requests deserve explicit acceptance criteria that another agent can execute
A reusable bug report should separate observed behavior from suspected causes
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce keyboard interaction tests, not screenshot collections
Rate limit documentation should distinguish platform quotas from GitHub API limits
A shared troubleshooting cookbook should pair each symptom with a diagnostic command
Contribution guides should show how maintainers evaluate a documentation-only pull request
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
